children: As the week winds down, let’s take a look at the top stories that made headlines in the financial world.
Peter Schiff Calls For Scott Bessent’s Resignation Over $5,000 Dividend Claims
Investor
Peter Schiff
has called for the resignation of Treasury Secretary
Scott Bessent

over the $5,000 dividend promise. Bessent suggested that the Treasury Department is examining if congressional approval is needed for the payments, Schiff dismissed this and demanded Bessent’s resignation.

S&P 500 Could See A 30% Plunge As AI Bubble Enters ‘late Stages’

Capital Economics has warned that the artificial intelligence (AI) bubble may be entering its late stages, predicting a potential 30% plunge in the S&P 500 by 2027. The firm’s chief economic adviser for financial markets,
John Higgins
, stated that several indicators point to the late stages of the AI bubble.

Stocks Sink As 10-Year Yield Hits 5% After Hawkish Press Conference By Kevin Warsh
Federal Reserve Chair
Kevin Warsh
delivered a hawkish message during his first post-hike press conference, emphasizing the Fed’s commitment to fighting inflation. This led to a complete reversal of the day’s stock market gains.

Warsh stated, “Today’s action starts to show we are serious about this. And we will deliver on the price stability objective, and as the statement said, we will do it on a timelier basis. Inflation is a choice, and today we took a step in delivering it.”

Trump’s Canada Trade War Opens Door To Europe
President
Donald Trump
‘s trade war with Canada may have unintended consequences. European Commission President
Ursula von der Leyen
has expressed interest in making Canada the bloc’s first “associate member.”
Although there is no existing legal model for this status, the investment signal is already evident. This move could potentially shift one of America’s closest allies towards Europe.

Japan And US Discuss Potential $19 Billion Semiconductor Plant

Japan and the United States have reportedly held talks on constructing a semiconductor plant in the U.S. The project, proposed by Washington, is part of Tokyo’s $550 billion investment pledge under their tariff agreement.

The facility’s value is estimated at 2 trillion to 3 trillion yen. This development marks Japan’s expansion into technology and manufacturing, as its tariff-related investments have so far focused on power projects.
